ambiguities.text: The specific reentrancy attack vector that necessitated EIP-1283 removal is not detailed in this EIP.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the attack involves contracts that relied on transfer gas stipends being insufficient for storage writes, which EIP-1283 would have violated. Consult EIP-1283 security analysis for details.

ambiguities.text: The meaning of 'Petersburg takes priority' when forks activate at same block is implied but not formally specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume Petersburg is processed after Constantinople in the fork ordering, effectively overriding EIP-1283 inclusion.

implicit_assumptions.description: All client implementations will correctly implement the fork precedence logic when Petersburg and Constantinople share the same activation block.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Consensus split between clients that enable vs disable EIP-1283, leading to chain fork.

implicit_assumptions.description: Node operators will upgrade to Petersburg-aware clients before block 7,280,000.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Non-upgraded nodes will fork off on a separate chain with EIP-1283 enabled.
